title: Training Values Based Education
text:
VALUES BASED EDUCATION PAPER
PRESENTED DURING THE MASTER
TRAINERS TRAINING AT CEMASTEA
 DEC 2019
 GRACE NGUGI MAINA.

 Kenyans that show low levels of values? Why ?
 INTRODUCTION
• In Kenya, there is a noticeable values and behavioural crisis among the general
 population and young people in particular.
• Many youngsters are growing up without the desired values, positive attitudes and
 psychosocial competencies needed to function as responsible citizens.
• The primary responsibility for nurturing values rests with parents and the community,
 but education too has an important role to play in this regard.
• The BECF recognizes that values are important to the socio-economic development
 and stability of the country, in the same way that competencies in academics are
 important.
• The Basic education curriculum framework, vision and mission are
 supported by three important pillars; Values, Theoretical approaches and
 Guiding principles.
• Values are also stipulated in the CBC Vision. An Engage, Empowered and
 Ethical citizen
• Values are also explicitly and implicitly highlighted in the National goals of
 Education and in the level outcomes in the EYE and middle school
 general. A good number of Learning areas have expected learning
 outcomes that focus on values or character formation of the learner.
 Meaning of Values
• Values are defined as standards that guide an individual on how to respond or
 behave in a given circumstance. They influence how we feel, act and make
 choices in life.
• In Sub-Saharan Africa, scholars have argued that the way ethnic groups interact
 has been responsible for Africa’s low economic growth, political instability and
 conflict, high inequality, and low provision of public goods.
• The teaching of values will facilitate the achievement of the curriculum reforms'
 vision, particularly with respect to moulding ethical citizens.
 OVERALL GOAL of values based education
• To nurture values in learners to become
 empowered, engaged and ethical citizens for
 positive and holistic transformation of society.
GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR VALUE BASED EDUCATION
Value based education aims to enable the learner to:
a) Possess a secure sense of personal identity for self-fulfilment and development.
b) Demonstrate cultural, moral and religious consciousness in their day to day life.
c) Demonstrate empathy and respect for diverse groups of people for harmonious
 relationships
a) Practice ethical behaviour to foster responsible citizenship and good
 governance.
b) Apply critical thinking and creative growth mind set thinking skills in finding
 ethical solutions to challenges in society.
c) Demonstrate stewardship of resources and environment for sustainable
 development

GUIDING PRINCIPLES FOR VALUES BASED EDUCATION
• 1.Whole School Approach (WSA)
• VBE will be implemented through whole-school approach which:
 involves learners, teachers, support staff, Board of Management,
 family members, wider school community and relevant stakeholders.
• VBE will be mainstreamed in the formal, non-formal informal
 dimensions of education, pedagogy, curriculum materials, co-
 curricular activities, instructional supervision and teacher
 management, schools policies.
VBE thro the WSA is a strategy that recognizes the effectiveness of
 mobilizing the entire school community and its resources towards improving
 the wellbeing of the learner and the community.
Sensitization of parents on VBE is key in ensuring that parents: demonstrate
 value-based behavior at home and create a secure and safe home environment.
Schools must practice what they teach; values and social skills are reinforced
 in action and consequently caught rather than taught.
 2.Holistic approach
• VBE adopts a holistic approach in its implementation
• It aims to support the learner to develop physically, spiritually,
 socially, intellectually and emotionally.
• This will thus call for interdisciplinary approach in the delivery.
3.Learning environment
• VBE should be implemented in a safe, supportive and conducive
 learning environment supported by a caring community.
• Every child shall learn in an environment that is socially
 facilitative, physically supportive and safe, emotionally secure and
 psychologically enabling.
 4.Capacity Building
• Values Based Education will be delivered by trained and resourced
 persons who can use appropriate and variety of approaches.
• They will require continuous professional development & adequate
 resourcing of all stakeholders for efficient and effective
 implementation
 5.Relevance to local and global perspectives
• Values Based Education will operate under a framework of
 common conceptual understanding.
• Therefore, it shall respect the learners age & grade levels; local,
 national & global contexts; while adopting ethical and healthy
 practices.
 6.Transformative Leadership
• The success of Values Based Education requires visionary,
 committed & inspiring leadership at all levels of the education
 system.
• Such leadership will model and consistently articulate the Values
 as an everyday practice.
 7.Monitoring, Evaluation, Research & Learning
• VBE recognizes that the context within which
 it is implemented is dynamic.
• There will be need for continuous monitoring,
 evaluation, research & learning for
 enrichment & improvement.
CORE VALUES
LOVE
• The family and school community have an obligation to
 create an environment where children feel loved and
 appreciated
RESPONSIBILITY
• The family & school community have an obligation to
 Respect
 • Respect is having positive regard towards
 self and others without prejudice.
 • A respectful person exhibits a level of open-
 mindedness and willingness to understand
 and appreciate others.
UNITY
• Unity is the ability to live together harmoniously regardless of social, cultural,
 racial, religious, economic and political differences.
• It is the recognition of the importance of working with other people towards a
 common goal.
• Nurturing the Value of unity among learners and members of school community
 will enhance togetherness and unity of purpose regardless of their diverse
 backgrounds
  Peace
• Peace is a state of tranquility & harmony with oneself & among
 people.
• The Value of peace enables an individual to remain calm always
 regardless of the circumstances around them.
• The Value of peace fosters self- awareness and esteem; healthy
 relationships and collaboration amongst people
  Patriotism
• Patriotism refers to loyalty, love and devotion for one’s country or
 nation.
• A patriotic individual is proud of their country, readily and
 competently performs their duties as a citizen.
• Patriotism calls for readiness to defend one’s country, obey its laws
 and respect fellow citizens.
• Parents, teachers and other adults in the community should model
 and nurture patriotism in children.
  Social Justice
• Social justice refers to fair treatment of each other and promotion of equity. It is
 about creating a society that is based on the principles of respect for human
 dignity, equity, solidarity and elimination of inequalities.
• It calls for fair and proper administration of laws and privileges to people
 irrespective prejudices such as ethnicity, age, gender, status, race, or religion.
• Vbe will foster fairness and justice among members of the school community
 thereby enabling the learners to be agents and advocates of social justice for
 harmonious relationships in the society.
  Integrity
• Integrity implies the ability to know, defend and do what is
 right always.
• A person of integrity exhibits commitment, courage and
 honesty and ethical conduct.
• For learners to nurture the Value of integrity, adults at home,
 school and wider community should model virtues such as
 honesty,discipline, transparency, fairness, accountability,
 consistency, reliability& humility.
 Conclusion
Indeed ,we should take advantage of the fact that learners
spend most of their formative years in school, which
presents opportunities for the curriculum to mould and
reinforce values upon which the learner’s character is
formed.
THE END!
